messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sustained org-level QPS spike detected (org: aurora-finance, org_id: org-742). Backend queues spiking, 5xxs up from 0.4% -> 3.9% over 4m. Auto-mitigation: global prefetch backoff ON, per-org soft-limit enforcement scheduled. Paging on-call SRE.

sre-lex: ack paging. I'm taking this. Looking at tail of requests now, many requests hitting streaming/generation path with 2k+ token contexts.

maya-eng: looking at runtime metrics — KV cache thrash + memory pressure on pool gpu-3a. A few hot customer prefixes causing big KV growth.

emily-cs: FYI aurora-finance is in our enterprise tier and they just reported timeouts to their platform team. They're asking for a quick fix, very high impact. 

sre-lex: understood. Proposed mitigations: 1) apply org-specific token-rate cap (lower their per-org burst) to protect cluster; 2) route AuroraFinance to a heavier but lower-latency model variant we have warmed (fallback-smaller) OR serve them on reserve capacity if they want a short emergency uplift. Thoughts?

jordan-prod: priority = enterprise SLA. If routing to fallback preserves uptime without data exposure change, that is preferred to bumping global capacity. Can we do hot route change?

maya-eng: yes, we have a warmed small-variant (rwd-small-v1) in the same region. Routing change is a config flip: toggle route table entry for org-742 to model=rwd-small-v1. I can do it, but need an ops approval because it touches routing policy.

sre-lex: do we have any short-term rate-limit action available? I can apply a temporary per-org shaping rule to smooth spikes: set org-742 max concurrent requests 40, token rps 12000 for 10m and watch. That reduces tail pressure.

emily-cs: aurora team prefers fallback routing > throttling if it avoids errors. But they asked if we can give them an emergency dedicated window for 30m to clear backlog. They said they'd accept the fallback if not possible.

sre-lex: plan: (A) apply conservative shaping now (concurrent=40, token-rps cap=12000) to protect cluster — will not fully cut them off; (B) immediately flip routing for org-742 -> rwd-small-v1 with a staged canary (5% -> 50% -> 100% over 2m) so we can measure latency/5xx; (C) if fallback fails, we can stand up a temporary quota increase on reserved pool for 30m (manual uplift).

maya-eng: executing route canary now. Command: ```/deploy route set --org org-742 --model rwd-small-v1 --canary 5%```

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: route-change-canary-4987654321. Started by maya-eng. Logs: https://deploys.internal/route-change-canary-4987654321

sre-lex: applying shaping rule now: ```/rl set --org org-742 --max-concurrent 40 --token-rps 12000 --duration 10m --reason \"mitigate cluster KV thrash\"``` 

deploy-bot: rate-limit rule applied: rl-rule-9872 for org-742 (expires in 10m).

maya-eng: canary metrics: after 90s 5xx for org-742 down from 3.9% -> 0.8%, median p95 latency down 220ms -> 130ms. No obvious downstream degradation. Increasing canary to 50%.

emily-cs: Aurora team confirms they can tolerate rwd-small-v1 for now. They asked to keep us posted. :thumbsup:

sre-lex: increasing canary to 50% done. Monitoring. If stable after next 2m we'll cutover.

maya-eng: cutover to 100% complete. Notes: KV pressure reduced, overall cluster error rate back to baseline 0.45%. Keeping the temporary shaping rule active for a full 10m window.

emily-cs: update to customer: \"We've routed your traffic to a lower-latency fallback model and applied temporary smoothing to avoid timeouts. Monitoring closely; you should see requests succeed now.\"

sre-lex: mitigation successful. No further paging. Action items: 1) revoke rl-rule-9872 when timer expires, 2) leave a pre-empt rollback play if errors spike again, 3) schedule a postmortem to analyze hot prefixes and consider prefix caching or per-prefix quotas.

jordan-prod: scheduling postmortem tomorrow 10:30 PT. Emily to coordinate customer-facing summary.

emily-cs: will send a short incident note to Aurora and include timeline.

sre-lex: closing thread, marking incident as mitigated. :white_check_mark:
